G2-MED-03.lead_in: What is the most appropriate next step in his management?

options.label: A
options.rationale: Inferior ST-elevation with hypotension, a raised jugular venous pressure and clear lungs is right-ventricular infarction physiology, which is preload dependent. CLM-ACS-RV-INFARCTION-STABILIZATION-01 directs cautious intravenous volume with reassessment of fluid responsiveness, and warns against preload-reducing therapy, while reperfusion proceeds.
options.text: Give a cautious intravenous fluid bolus and reassess fluid responsiveness

options.label: B
options.rationale: Live: A candidate who treats a raised jugular venous pressure as fluid overload without checking the lungs will remove the preload the right ventricle depends on. Inferior: Correct where the raised filling pressure is accompanied by pulmonary congestion in a patient who is not preload dependent. That condition is not met here.
options.text: Give intravenous furosemide for the raised jugular venous pressure

options.label: C
options.rationale: Live: A candidate reciting the early infarct bundle may add beta blockade without asking whether the output state permits it. Inferior: Correct after stabilization, once the patient is out of a low-output state and is not at risk of cardiogenic shock. That condition is not met here.
options.text: Give intravenous metoprolol to reduce myocardial oxygen demand

options.label: D
options.rationale: Live: A candidate applying the general infarct algorithm rather than reading the right-ventricular physiology will give the nitrate that the algorithm lists first. Inferior: Correct for ischaemic pain in a patient whose physiology is not preload dependent and who is not hypotensive. That condition is not met here.
options.text: Give sublingual nitroglycerin for the ischaemic pain

options.label: E
options.rationale: Live: A candidate who equates a low blood pressure with cardiogenic shock will escalate to a vasopressor before trying the preload correction the physiology calls for. Inferior: Correct where acute-myocardial-infarction cardiogenic shock is present, that is persistent hypotension or a vasopressor requirement with end-organ hypoperfusion, alongside emergency revascularization. That condition is not met here.

G2-MED-03.stem: A 64-year-old man is brought to the emergency department 90 minutes after the sudden onset of crushing retrosternal pain with nausea and sweating. His blood pressure is 84/56 mmHg and his heart rate is 58 beats per minute. His jugular venous pressure is elevated to 8 cm above the sternal angle and his lung fields are clear throughout on auscultation. The electrocardiogram shows 3 mm of ST-segment elevation in leads II, III and aVF with reciprocal ST depression in I and aVL. High-sensitivity troponin is 480 ng/L on arrival and 2,900 ng/L on the repeat sample drawn one hour later. The interventional team has been activated and the catheterisation laboratory will be ready to receive him in 25 minutes.

G2-OBGYN-01.lead_in: What is the most likely diagnosis?

options.label: A
options.rationale: CLM-R2-OB-MASTITIS-ANCHOR defines inflammatory and bacterial mastitis as an increasingly erythematous, oedematous and painful region of the breast with systemic signs such as fever and chills. A firm mass-like area without fluctuance is inflammation, not a drainable collection.

options.label: B
options.rationale: Live: A candidate who reaches for the retained-milk explanation for any lactational lump. Inferior: Correct for a moderately firm mass without erythema or systemic symptoms, decreasing temporarily after a feed. That condition is not met here.

options.label: C
options.rationale: Live: A candidate who has been taught never to miss the malignant mimic and applies it without its stated skin findings. Inferior: Correct with skin thickening, breast retraction and a peau d'orange appearance, or with recurrence in the same location. That condition is not met here.

options.label: D
options.rationale: Live: A candidate who escalates to the more serious entity on the spectrum without requiring the fluid collection that defines it. Inferior: Correct where a palpable fluid collection is present in a well-defined area of the breast. That condition is not met here.

G2-OBGYN-01.stem: A 29-year-old woman is seen twelve days after an uncomplicated vaginal delivery. She is breastfeeding and for the past two days the upper outer part of her left breast has become increasingly painful. On examination that segment of the breast is red, swollen and tender, and within it there is a firm mass-like area with no fluctuance. Her temperature is 38.6 degrees Celsius and she has had rigors and generalised aching since yesterday.

G2-PED-01.lead_in: What is the most likely diagnosis?

options.label: A
options.rationale: A first wheezing episode in an infant under twelve months following a two-to-three-day coryzal prodrome is the phenotype CLM-R2-PED-DX-ANCHOR defines as bronchiolitis. Atopy and an asymmetric area of reduced air entry do not displace it.

options.label: B
options.rationale: Live: A candidate who treats any crackle plus fever as evidence of air-space consolidation, and who does not know that patchy hyperinflation and atelectasis in this illness are routinely misread as consolidation. Inferior: Correct where the illness is not improving as expected, where severity raises the possibility of bacterial infection, or where a focal consolidation is demonstrated. That condition is not met here.

options.label: C
options.rationale: Live: A candidate who recognises reversible lower airway obstruction but does not apply the age and first-episode conditions that separate the two. Inferior: Correct in an older infant or child with frequent recurrences, atopy, or wheeze without a viral upper respiratory prodrome. That condition is not met here.

options.label: D
options.rationale: Live: A candidate who knows aspiration must always be considered in a wheezing infant but does not weigh the prodrome or the symmetry of the examination. Inferior: Correct where the onset is abrupt without a viral prodrome, or where findings are focal or asymmetric. That condition is not met here.

G2-PED-01.stem: A 7-month-old girl is brought to the emergency department because of noisy breathing that started today. For the past three days she has had a runny nose, a cough and a temperature up to 37.9 degrees Celsius. This is the first time she has ever wheezed. She has eczema and her mother has asthma. Her respiratory rate is 56 breaths per minute and her oxygen saturation is 95 per cent in room air. There is subcostal indrawing, with widespread expiratory wheeze and crackles, and air entry at the right base is reduced compared with the left.

G2-PED-02.lead_in: Which assessment is most appropriate for this infant on the ward?

options.label: A
options.rationale: Live: A candidate who wants radiographic confirmation before committing to a clinical diagnosis, not knowing that the film in this illness is routinely misread as consolidation. Inferior: Correct where the diagnosis is unclear, improvement is not as expected, or severity raises the possibility of bacterial pneumonia. That condition is not met here.

options.label: B
options.rationale: Live: A candidate who correctly knows saturation matters in this illness, and who does not know that the guideline reserves continuous monitoring for high-risk infants early in the course and warns that it prolongs stay. Inferior: Correct for a high-risk patient early in the course of the disease. That condition is not met here.
options.text: Continuous pulse oximetry and cardiorespiratory monitoring

options.label: C
options.rationale: Live: A candidate who equates identifying the organism with making the diagnosis. Inferior: Correct where testing is required for infection control purposes, or in a high risk patient where the result will influence treatment. That condition is not met here.

options.label: D
options.rationale: CLM-R2-PED-INV-ANCHOR states diagnostic studies are not indicated for most children with bronchiolitis, and CLM-R4-PED-MONITORING states that regular repeated clinical assessment by staff with appropriate expertise is the most important component of monitoring and that electronic monitoring is not a substitute for it. CLM-R4-PED-CONTINUOUS reserves continuous saturation monitoring for high-risk patients early in the course.
options.text: Regular clinical assessment with intermittent oximetry

G2-PED-02.stem: A 5-month-old boy was admitted to the paediatric ward yesterday with bronchiolitis, on the fourth day of an illness that began with coryza, cough and fever. Overnight his oxygen saturation fell to 89 per cent in room air and low-flow oxygen by nasal prongs was started. This morning his work of breathing and his feeding are much the same as they were on admission rather than better. The ward is full, and the bed manager needs to know whether he can be cohorted in a bay with the other infants who have already tested positive for respiratory syncytial virus.

G2-PHELO-01.lead_in: Which explanation best accounts for this pattern of results?

options.label: A
options.rationale: Live: A candidate who defaults to selection bias whenever screened and unscreened groups are compared. Inferior: Correct where the compared groups self-selected and differ in baseline health. That condition is not met here.

options.label: B
options.rationale: CLM-R2-PHELO-LEAD-TIME states that lead-time bias arises from the delay between detectability by screening and the point at which disease would be diagnosed without screening, and that evaluating a programme by survival time after diagnosis may give a falsely positive impression of success. Longer survival from diagnosis with unchanged disease-specific mortality in a randomised comparison is exactly that pattern.

options.label: C
options.rationale: Live: A candidate who has learned the two biases as a pair and cannot separate them without deliberately checking whether the disease mix or the diagnosis date moved. Inferior: Correct where the screened group contains a disproportionate share of slowly progressing variants of the disease. That condition is not met here.

options.label: D
options.rationale: Live: A candidate who knows overdiagnosis is the fashionable screening critique and reaches for it whenever survival improves without mortality falling. Inferior: Correct where more cases are diagnosed in the screened group than in the unscreened group. That condition is not met here.

G2-PHELO-01.stem: A trial randomly allocated 60,000 adults either to be invited to a screening programme for a solid tumour or to usual care. The two groups were comparable at baseline in age, sex and smoking history. After twelve years of follow-up, median survival measured from the date of diagnosis was 5.8 years among those diagnosed in the invited group and 3.1 years among those diagnosed in the usual-care group. Over the same period there were 412 deaths from the tumour in the invited group and 419 in the usual-care group, a difference the investigators report as not statistically significant.

G2-PHELO-02.lead_in: Which revision to the letter would best protect the autonomy of the people invited?

options.label: A
options.rationale: Live: A candidate who equates autonomy with voluntariness, rather than with the quality of the information on which a choice is made, will select the edit that names consent explicitly. Inferior: Correct where the letter's defect is that readers feel obliged to attend, rather than that the benefit is stated in a form they cannot interpret. That condition is not met here.
options.text: Add a statement that participation is voluntary and that declining will not affect any other care

options.label: B
options.rationale: Live: A candidate who equates disclosing a number with informed consent and does not ask whether the number tells the reader anything about their own risk. Inferior: Correct where the reader also has the denominator and the harms, so the figure can be interpreted. That condition is not met here.
options.text: Add the number of cancers the programme detected last year

options.label: C
options.rationale: Live: A candidate who treats completeness of technical information as equivalent to informed choice. Inferior: Correct as programme documentation, where the audience can interpret the figures. That condition is not met here.
options.text: Add the sensitivity and specificity of the screening test

options.label: D
options.rationale: CLM-R4-PHELO-ABSOLUTE states that a relative statement sounds impressive but may not help an individual, who would benefit more from an absolute figure. Where the declared purpose is an informed decision rather than uptake, replacing the relative figure with the absolute chance of benefit and the chance of a false positive is the revision that serves it.
options.text: Replace the relative figure with the absolute benefit and the chance of a false positive

G2-PHELO-02.stem: A provincial screening programme is revising the letter it sends to invite people to a first screening test. The programme's steering committee has recorded that the purpose of the revision is to help each person invited make the decision that is right for them, and explicitly not to increase the number who attend. The current letter explains what the test involves and where to attend, and the only thing it says about what the programme achieves is that screening reduces deaths from the disease by 25 per cent.

G2-PHELO-03.lead_in: What should the programme do about the planned launch?

options.label: A
options.rationale: CLM-R2-PHELO-FACILITIES states that if waiting lists are long or facilities for follow-up and treatment are not conveniently accessible, the screening programme should be reconsidered. A confirmatory pathway with a nine-month wait and no additional capacity, and no treatment capacity at all, is that situation.
options.text: Defer the launch until diagnostic and treatment capacity is in place

options.label: B
options.rationale: Live: A candidate who selects the option carrying a recognised programme criterion without asking whether the criterion addresses the specific shortfall described. Inferior: Correct as a standing requirement of any programme that does launch. That condition is not met here.
options.text: Launch as planned with continuing evaluation against programme goals

options.label: C
options.rationale: Live: A candidate who reaches for staged rollout as the generic answer to any capacity constraint without asking whether the bottleneck scales down with the volume. Inferior: Correct where the constraint is cost or logistics rather than an absolute shortfall in the confirmatory pathway. That condition is not met here.
options.text: Launch in a single district as a pilot and expand later

options.label: D
options.rationale: Live: A candidate who solves the capacity arithmetic and does not price the missed cases on the other side of the trade-off. Inferior: Correct where the current threshold sits too far toward the low-risk end and is generating avoidable low-yield referrals. That condition is not met here.
options.text: Raise the threshold so that fewer results are called positive

G2-PHELO-03.stem: A regional health authority is four weeks away from launching a population screening programme for a treatable cancer. The programme has written goals, a defined target population, and an evaluation plan with agreed indicators and a first report due at eighteen months. The single specialist centre that would perform the confirmatory diagnostic procedure has no additional capacity and its current wait is nine months, and the two surgeons who would treat screen-detected disease are already fully booked, with no further staff or operating time identified anywhere in the region.

G2-PSY-03.lead_in: Which initial treatment should be offered?

options.label: A
options.rationale: CLM-R2-PSY-MODERATE-CHOICE makes structured psychotherapy and antidepressant medication the two initial options for a moderate episode and equally effective in the short term. Where in-person structured psychotherapy is not deliverable, CLM-R2-PSY-FIRST-LINE supports a first-line antidepressant as the initial treatment that can actually be started.

options.label: B
options.rationale: Live: A candidate who reads first-line monotherapy without the severity qualifier attached to it. Inferior: Correct as first-line monotherapy for mild depression, and as a second-line adjunct at moderate severity. That condition is not met here.
options.text: A supervised exercise programme as sole initial treatment

options.label: C
options.rationale: Live: A candidate who spots the access constraint, solves it with the digital format, and does not notice that the patient's preference, not access, is what selects the modality. Inferior: Correct where psychotherapy is the chosen modality and in-person delivery is not available. That condition is not met here.

options.label: D
options.rationale: Live: A candidate who remembers that psychotherapy is preferred at the lower severities and generalises that preference upward without reading the preference and access conditions. Inferior: Correct where the patient prefers it and it is readily accessible, and preferred at mild severity. That condition is not met here.
options.text: Structured psychotherapy such as cognitive behavioural therapy

G2-PSY-03.stem: A 34-year-old woman describes two months of low mood, loss of interest in things she used to enjoy, early morning waking and difficulty concentrating. She has stopped going to her book club and has fallen behind at work, although she is still attending. On assessment she has no thoughts of harming herself and no plan or intent, and she has good support from her partner and her sister. Her physician assesses the episode as of moderate severity. She lives in a rural community where the nearest in-person structured psychotherapy service has a waiting list of more than a year and no therapist practises locally.

G2-SURG-01.lead_in: What is the most likely diagnosis?

options.label: A
options.rationale: CLM-R4-SURG-PRESENTATION gives the classic sequence: pain beginning periumbilically and migrating to the right lower quadrant, with anorexia, vomiting, low-grade fever and localised right lower quadrant tenderness.

options.label: B
options.rationale: Live: A candidate who has been taught never to miss torsion in a young woman with acute pelvic pain and treats severity and vomiting as sufficient grounds. Inferior: Correct where there is an adnexal mass of five centimetres or more, or intermittent severe pain with a poorly localised or absent tenderness pattern. That condition is not met here.

options.label: C
options.rationale: Live: A candidate who knows that pelvic inflammatory disease must always be considered in a young woman with lower abdominal pain and fever, and who applies that rule without testing the pelvic examination findings the syndrome requires. Inferior: Correct where the pelvic examination shows cervical motion tenderness or adnexal tenderness with lower abdominal tenderness. That condition is not met here.

options.label: D
options.rationale: Live: A candidate who reads fever plus unilateral pelvic pain as a walled-off pelvic infection and does not weigh the tempo of the illness. Inferior: Correct where the pain has been more gradual in onset with the pelvic findings of upper genital tract infection. That condition is not met here.

G2-SURG-01.stem: A 24-year-old woman presents with 18 hours of abdominal pain. The pain began around the umbilicus and over the last several hours has settled in the right lower quadrant. She has no appetite and vomited once this morning. Her last menstrual period was two weeks ago and a urine pregnancy test is negative. Her temperature is 37.6 degrees Celsius and there is tenderness with voluntary guarding in the right lower quadrant.

G2-SURG-02.lead_in: What is the most appropriate next step in diagnosis?

options.label: A
options.rationale: Live: A candidate who correctly prefers to avoid ionising radiation and does not apply the body-habitus condition attached to that preference. Inferior: Correct in a low body mass index patient, and as the first modality in pregnancy. That condition is not met here.

options.label: B
options.rationale: Live: A candidate who knows that serial examination is a legitimate surgical tool and applies it before the imaging step it is meant to follow. Inferior: Correct after non-diagnostic imaging, where clinical suspicion on reassessment is intermediate or low. That condition is not met here.
options.text: Admit for serial abdominal examination without imaging

options.label: C
options.rationale: CLM-R2-SURG-ALVARADO places intermediate clinical suspicion in the band for which computed tomography is recommended, and CLM-R2-SURG-CT records its reported sensitivity of 90.4 to 100 per cent and specificity of 94 per cent, its wide availability and its ease of interpretation.

options.label: D
options.rationale: Live: A candidate who ranks modalities by sensitivity and specificity and ignores the indication and availability conditions. Inferior: Correct in pregnancy when ultrasound is non-definitive. That condition is not met here.
options.text: Magnetic resonance imaging of the abdomen

options.label: E
options.rationale: Live: A candidate who has anchored on the wrong diagnosis and then chooses that diagnosis's correct first test. Inferior: Correct where a ureteral stone is the leading diagnosis. That condition is not met here.
options.text: Ultrasonography with a plain kidney-ureter-bladder film

G2-SURG-02.stem: A 41-year-old man has had 24 hours of right lower quadrant pain with anorexia and one episode of vomiting. His temperature is 37.4 degrees Celsius and his white cell count is 11.2 x 10^9/L. There is tenderness in the right lower quadrant but no guarding and no rebound. After assessing him the surgical resident judges the probability of appendicitis to be intermediate: not low enough to send him home and not high enough to take him to the operating room. He has normal renal function and no allergies. Both computed tomography and ultrasonography are available in the department without delay.

option_contract: Every option resolves to the key or to a row of the contrast matrix. The option layer composes rationales from matrix fields and adds no clinical claim of its own.
